goal: Turn large public corpora into compact reusable structured features while minimizing user interaction, machine-local work, and paid compute.

execution_planes.private_local_state: OSR Watcher on Mac only when genuinely required

primary_product.output: versioned sparse Feature Store in Parquet + compact feature catalog
layers: F0 shard structural features over the complete corpus
F2 selective deep entity/event extraction over high-signal rows only

supported_now.output: Parquet feature-store partitions + compact JSON feature catalog
edge/node candidate tables for downstream review

examples: q-gram locator for repeated query families

not_default.reason: Quickwit/Tantivy pilot expanded sampled text by 6.1566x; 508GB is not large enough, and the research workload is not search-heavy enough, to justify Elasticsearch/Quickwit deployment overhead
Operational complexity and persistent storage are unnecessary at this corpus scale and workload shape; search is an auxiliary locator problem, not the primary product
3-gram pilot expanded sampled text by 1.8198x; useful only for repeated high-value query families
Deep NER/LLM inference over every byte is economically wasteful. Full-corpus extraction is shallow/deterministic; deep extraction is routed only to high-signal rows.
Mac+rclone measured only 1.7-2.4 MiB/s and adds user-machine dependency
raw data remains upstream; runners use ephemeral shard hydration and persist only compact derivatives

current_priority: validate feature-store-v1-smoke-001 on two real shards
scale Feature Store v1 to all 1788 shards with 20 workers after smoke passes
persist worker feature partitions and compact catalog
build selective F2 entity/event extractor over F1 high-signal rows
derive graph and aggregation layers from Feature Store rather than repeatedly scanning raw corpus
economic_rule: Prefer feature backfill and selective deep extraction over persistent universal search infrastructure; build an index only when repeated lookup savings exceed storage and operational cost.
evidence_rule: Every derived feature must retain source corpus, shard, row or equivalent locator, and hash/provenance sufficient for exact source recheck.
